section_1.title: The Hook: The Whistle-Bot's Pure Tones
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of complex periodic signals by using a 'Whistle-Bot' character. Explain that while most sounds are messy, the Whistle-Bot only understands pure, smooth oscillations (Sines and Cosines). The goal is to recreate a jagged 'Square Wave' jump using only these smooth movements.
section_1.example: Visualizing a Whistle-Bot moving up and down in a jerky square pattern, then overlaying smooth sine waves to show the approximation.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Full Fourier Recipe
section_2.content: Briefly review the Standard Fourier Series formula. Explain that any periodic function f(x) is a 'stew' of a constant (a0), Cosines (an), and Sines (bn). Emphasize the concept of 'Orthogonality'—that sines and cosines are like independent building blocks that don't mix.
section_2.example: An animation of a kitchen blender where 'Cosine Carrots' and 'Sine Spinneys' are tossed in to create a 'Function Soup'.

section_3.title: The Symmetry Filter: Even and Odd Functions
section_3.content: Introduce symmetry as a way to simplify the 'stew'. Define Even functions (f(x) = f(-x)) as mirror reflections across the Y-axis and Odd functions (f(x) = -f(-x)) as rotational symmetry. Explain that Cosine is the 'Even King' and Sine is the 'Odd Queen'.
section_3.example: A 'Symmetry Cat' sitting on the Y-axis. If the cat looks at a mirror and sees itself exactly, it's Even (Cosine-like). If it sees itself upside down on the other side, it's Odd (Sine-like).

section_4.title: Deriving the Pure Sine Series
section_4.content: Explain that if a function is Odd, all 'Even' components (Cosines) must have coefficients of zero (an = 0). This results in a 'Pure Sine Series'. Show the simplified integral formula for bn, noting that we only need to integrate over half the period (0 to L) and multiply by 2.
section_4.example: A visual 'mathematical sieve' where a jagged Odd Wave passes through, trapping all Cosine terms in the mesh and letting only Sine terms flow through to the final equation.

section_5.title: Deriving the Pure Cosine Series
section_5.content: Conversely, if the function is Even, all 'Odd' components (Sines) vanish (bn = 0). This creates a 'Pure Cosine Series'. Highlight that the constant term a0 (the average value) remains here because a constant is also an 'Even' function.
section_5.example: A graph of a 'Tent Map' function (Even). Watch the Sine waves try to fit but fail due to symmetry, leaving only the 'flat' a0 and the 'peaky' Cosines to reconstruct the shape.

section_6.title: Application: Building the Square Wave
section_6.content: Step-by-step calculation of a Pure Sine Series for a Square Wave (an Odd function). Show how adding the 1st, 3rd, and 5th harmonics gradually transforms a smooth wave into a sharp square corner.
section_6.example: An animation of the 'Square-Wave Robot' from Section 1. As we add more Sine terms (1/n terms), the robot's path becomes flatter on top and steeper at the edges, demonstrating the Gibbs Phenomenon at the corners.

section_7.title: Summary: Efficiency through Geometry
section_7.content: Wrap up by emphasizing that Pure Fourier Series aren't just 'shorter' math; they represent the inherent physical symmetry of a system (like a vibrating string fixed at both ends).
section_7.example: A split-screen view: One side shows a messy full equation, the other shows the elegant, 'Pure' version, highlighting the 50% reduction in computational effort.

section_3.example: A 'Symmetry Cat' sitting on the Y-axis. If the cat looks at a mirror and sees itself exactly, it's Even (Cosine-like). If it sees itself upside down on the other side, it's Odd (Sine-like).

section_4.title: Deriving the Pure Sine Series
section_4.content: Explain that if a function is Odd, all 'Even' components (Cosines) must have coefficients of zero (an = 0). This results in a 'Pure Sine Series'. Show the simplified integral formula for bn, noting that we only need to integrate over half the period (0 to L) and multiply by 2.
section_4.example: A visual 'mathematical sieve' where a jagged Odd Wave passes through, trapping all Cosine terms in the mesh and letting only Sine terms flow through to the final equation.

section_5.title: Deriving the Pure Cosine Series
section_5.content: Conversely, if the function is Even, all 'Odd' components (Sines) vanish (bn = 0). This creates a 'Pure Cosine Series'. Highlight that the constant term a0 (the average value) remains here because a constant is also an 'Even' function.
section_5.example: A graph of a 'Tent Map' function (Even). Watch the Sine waves try to fit but fail due to symmetry, leaving only the 'flat' a0 and the 'peaky' Cosines to reconstruct the shape.

section_6.title: Application: Building the Square Wave
section_6.content: Step-by-step calculation of a Pure Sine Series for a Square Wave (an Odd function). Show how adding the 1st, 3rd, and 5th harmonics gradually transforms a smooth wave into a sharp square corner.
section_6.example: An animation of the 'Square-Wave Robot' from Section 1. As we add more Sine terms (1/n terms), the robot's path becomes flatter on top and steeper at the edges, demonstrating the Gibbs Phenomenon at the corners.

section_7.title: Summary: Efficiency through Geometry
section_7.content: Wrap up by emphasizing that Pure Fourier Series aren't just 'shorter' math; they represent the inherent physical symmetry of a system (like a vibrating string fixed at both ends).
section_7.example: A split-screen view: One side shows a messy full equation, the other shows the elegant, 'Pure' version, highlighting the 50% reduction in computational effort.

section_1.title: The Hook: The Whistle-Bot's Pure Tones
lecture_lines: Meet Whistle-Bot, a master of pure periodic tones.
Most sounds are messy, but Whistle-Bot prefers smooth oscillations.
He moves in a jerky, jagged square wave pattern.
Can we recreate this jump using only smooth movements?
Let's explore the power of mathematical symmetry.
animations: Whistle-Bot moves in a jerky square pattern (#FFD700).
A single smooth Sine wave appears (#ADD8E6).
Whistle-Bot's path is overlaid with the Sine wave.
Second harmonic Sine wave joins the sum (#90EE90).
Resulting wave starts looking like the square path.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Full Fourier Recipe
lecture_lines: Every periodic function is a mathematical "stew" of waves.
The recipe includes constants, cosines, and sine components.
These building blocks are independent and do not mix.
animations: Full Fourier formula appears in the center (#FFFFFF).
Highlight a0 in yellow (#FFFF00).
Highlight Cosine terms in blue (#0000FF).
Highlight Sine terms in green (#00FF00).
Icons for Sine and Cosine remain separate (Orthogonality).

section_3.title: The Symmetry Filter: Even and Odd Functions
lecture_lines: Symmetry simplifies our mathematical "stew" significantly.
Even functions mirror perfectly across the vertical axis.
Odd functions exhibit rotational symmetry through the origin.
Cosines are the "Even Kings" of the wave world.
Sines serve as the "Odd Queens" in our series.
animations: Parabola y=x^2 mirrors across the Y-axis (#ADD8E6).
Cubic y=x^3 rotates 180 degrees through origin (#90EE90).
'Even King' Cosine graph flashes on the left (#ADD8E6).
'Odd Queen' Sine graph flashes on the right (#90EE90).

section_4.title: Deriving the Pure Sine Series
lecture_lines: For odd functions, all cosine terms vanish to zero.
We are left with a pure sine series representation.
Integration only requires half the period, then double it.
animations: Odd Square Wave enters a 'Cosine Filter' box (#FFFFFF).
Cosine terms (an) are ejected from the filter (#FF0000).
an = 0 text appears in bold (#FF0000).
Formula for bn fades in with 2/L highlighted (#FFFF00).

section_5.title: Deriving the Pure Cosine Series
lecture_lines: For even functions, all sine terms disappear completely.
This creates a pure cosine series for the function.
The constant average value, a0, remains an even component.
animations: Even Triangle Wave enters a 'Sine Filter' box (#FFFFFF).
Sine terms (bn) are ejected from the filter (#FF0000).
bn = 0 text appears in bold (#FF0000).
a0 (average value) stays with the Cosine terms (#FFFF00).

section_6.title: Application: Building the Square Wave
lecture_lines: Let's build a square wave using our sine series.
Adding the first harmonic creates a basic smooth curve.
Higher odd harmonics sharpen the corners of the wave.
With enough terms, a jagged square shape emerges.
Watch the "ears" appear at the edges—the Gibbs Phenomenon.
animations: Plot y = sin(x) (fundamental frequency) (#ADD8E6).
Add y = 1/3 sin(3x) to the graph (#90EE90).
Add y = 1/5 sin(5x) to the graph (#FFFF00).
Highlight the 'ripples' near the jump (Gibbs Phenomenon).

section_7.title: Summary: Efficiency through Geometry
lecture_lines: Pure series exploit the inherent symmetry of physical systems.
Symmetry reduces our computational work by half.
Elegant geometry makes complex math much more efficient.
animations: Left: Complex formula vs Right: Simple formula (#FFFFFF).
'50% Less Math' label appears on the right (#00FF00).
A vibrating string animation shows physical symmetry (#ADD8E6).
Closing text: 'Symmetry is efficiency' (#FFFFFF).

outline.title: The Symmetry Filter: Even and Odd Functions
outline.content: Introduce symmetry as a way to simplify the 'stew'. Define Even functions (f(x) = f(-x)) as mirror reflections across the Y-axis and Odd functions (f(x) = -f(-x)) as rotational symmetry. Explain that Cosine is the 'Even King' and Sine is the 'Odd Queen'.
outline.example: A 'Symmetry Cat' sitting on the Y-axis. If the cat looks at a mirror and sees itself exactly, it's Even (Cosine-like). If it sees itself upside down on the other side, it's Odd (Sine-like).

storyboard.title: The Symmetry Filter: Even and Odd Functions
lecture_lines: Symmetry simplifies our mathematical "stew" significantly.
Even functions mirror perfectly across the vertical axis.
Odd functions exhibit rotational symmetry through the origin.
Cosines are the "Even Kings" of the wave world.
Sines serve as the "Odd Queens" in our series.
animations: Parabola y=x^2 mirrors across the Y-axis (#ADD8E6).
Cubic y=x^3 rotates 180 degrees through origin (#90EE90).
'Even King' Cosine graph flashes on the left (#ADD8E6).
'Odd Queen' Sine graph flashes on the right (#90EE90).

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Deriving the Pure Cosine Series"
        lines = [
            "For even functions, all sine terms disappear completely.",
            "This creates a pure cosine series for the function.",
            "The constant average value, a0, remains an even component."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        filter_color = "#FFFFFF"
        bn_color = "#FF0000"
        a0_color = "#FFFF00"
        cosine_color = "#00FFFF" # Light cyan for cosines

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(filter_color))

        # Create Sine Filter Box
        filter_box = Rectangle(width=2, height=1.5, color=filter_color)
        filter_text = Text("Sine Filter", font_size=18, color=filter_color)
        sine_filter = VGroup(filter_box, filter_text)
        self.place_in_area(sine_filter, "B3", "D4")
        
        # Create Even Triangle Wave
        triangle_wave = VMobject(color=WHITE)
        triangle_wave.set_points_as_corners([
            [-0.5, -0.5, 0], [0, 0.5, 0], [0.5, -0.5, 0]
        ])
        self.place_at_grid(triangle_wave, "C2")

        self.play(FadeIn(sine_filter))
        self.play(FadeIn(triangle_wave))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Move triangle wave into filter
        self.play(
            triangle_wave.animate.move_to(sine_filter.get_center()).scale(0.5).set_alpha(0),
            run_time=1.5
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(bn_color))

        # Sine terms (bn) ejected from the filter
        sine_icon = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.3 * np.sin(2 * PI * x), x_range=[-0.5, 0.5], color=bn_color)
        bn_label = MathTex("b_n = 0", color=bn_color).scale(0.8)
        
        self.place_at_grid(sine_icon, "C4")
        self.place_at_grid(bn_label, "E4")

        # Animate ejection
        self.play(
            sine_icon.animate.move_to(self.grid["E4"]),
            FadeIn(bn_label, target_position=self.grid["E4"]),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(FadeOut(sine_icon))

        # Cosine terms emerge from the right
        cosine_icon = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.3 * np.cos(2 * PI * x), x_range=[-0.5, 0.5], color=cosine_color)
        self.place_at_grid(cosine_icon, "C5")
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(cosine_icon, shift=RIGHT),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(a0_color))

        # a0 remains with the cosine terms
        a0_label = MathTex("a_0", color=a0_color).scale(0.8)
        a0_line = Line(start=[-0.4, 0, 0], end=[0.4, 0, 0], color=a0_color)
        a0_group = VGroup(a0_line, a0_label).arrange(UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(a0_group, "D5")

        self.play(
            FadeIn(a0_group, shift=UP),
            cosine_icon.animate.shift(UP * 0.2), # Small adjustment to group them
            run_time=1
        )
        
        # Group result
        result_group = VGroup(cosine_icon, a0_group)
        rect_highlight = SurroundingRectangle(result_group, color=WHITE, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(rect_highlight))
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup data
        title = "Application: Building the Square Wave"
        lines = [
            "Let's build a square wave using our sine series.",
            "Adding the first harmonic creates a basic smooth curve.",
            "Higher odd harmonics sharpen the corners of the wave.",
            "With enough terms, a jagged square shape emerges.",
            "Watch the \"ears\" appear at the edges—the Gibbs Phenomenon."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_H1 = "#ADD8E6"  # Light Blue
        COLOR_H3 = "#90EE90"  # Light Green
        COLOR_H5 = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        COLOR_SUM = WHITE
        COLOR_GIBBS = RED

        # Axes setup
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-1.1 * PI, 1.1 * PI, PI / 2],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=4.0,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GRAY},
            tips=False
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "F6")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Let's build a square wave using our sine series."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(Create(axes), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Adding the first harmonic creates a basic smooth curve."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_H1)
        
        func_h1 = lambda x: np.sin(x)
        graph_current = axes.plot(func_h1, color=COLOR_H1)
        label_current = MathTex("S_1(x) = \\sin(x)", color=COLOR_H1, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(label_current, "A4")
        
        self.play(Create(graph_current), Write(label_current))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Higher odd harmonics sharpen the corners of the wave."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_H3)
        
        # Step 1: n=3
        func_h3 = lambda x: np.sin(x) + (1/3) * np.sin(3*x)
        graph_h3 = axes.plot(func_h3, color=COLOR_H3)
        label_h3 = MathTex("S_3(x) = \\sin(x) + \\frac{1}{3}\\sin(3x)", color=COLOR_H3, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(label_h3, "A4")
        
        self.play(
            Transform(graph_current, graph_h3),
            Transform(label_current, label_h3),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Step 2: n=5
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_H5)
        func_h5 = lambda x: np.sin(x) + (1/3) * np.sin(3*x) + (1/5) * np.sin(5*x)
        graph_h5 = axes.plot(func_h5, color=COLOR_H5)
        label_h5 = MathTex("S_5(x) = \\sum_{n=1,3,5} \\frac{1}{n}\\sin(nx)", color=COLOR_H5, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(label_h5, "A4")
        
        self.play(
            Transform(graph_current, graph_h5),
            Transform(label_current, label_h5),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "With enough terms, a jagged square shape emerges."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        
        def fourier_sum_n(x, n_max):
            return sum([(1/k) * np.sin(k*x) for k in range(1, n_max + 1, 2)])

        func_h19 = lambda x: fourier_sum_n(x, 19)
        graph_h19 = axes.plot(func_h19, color=COLOR_SUM)
        label_h19 = MathTex("S_{19}(x) = \\sum_{n=1,3,\\dots,19} \\frac{1}{n}\\sin(nx)", color=COLOR_SUM, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(label_h19, "A4")
        
        self.play(
            Transform(graph_current, graph_h19),
            Transform(label_current, label_h19),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "Watch the \"ears\" appear at the edges—the Gibbs Phenomenon."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_GIBBS)
        
        # Highlighting the overshoot "ears"
        ripples = VGroup(

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]

        graph_current = axes.plot(func_h1, color=COLOR_H1)

        )

        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_H5)

        graph_h5 = axes.plot(func_h5, color=COLOR_H5)

        self.place_at_grid(label_h5, "A4")
        
        self.play(
            Transform(graph_current, graph_h5),
            Transform(label_current, label_h5),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "With enough terms, a jagged square shape emerges."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        
        def fourier_sum_n(x, n_max):
            return sum([(1/k) * np.sin(k*x) for k in range(1, n_max + 1, 2)])

        func_h19 = lambda x: fourier_sum_n(x, 19)

        self.play(
            Transform(graph_current, graph_h19),
            Transform(label_current, label_h19),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "Watch the \"ears\" appear at the edges—the Gibbs Phenomenon."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_GIBBS)
        
        # Highlighting the overshoot "ears"
        ripples = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.15, color=COLOR_GIBBS).move_to(axes.c2p(0.1, 1.2)),
            Circle(radius=0.15, color=COLOR_GIBBS).move_to(axes.c2p(-0.1, -1.2)),
            Circle(radius=0.15, color=COLOR_GIBBS).move_to(axes.c2p(PI-0.1, 1.2)),

        gibbs_text = Text("Gibbs Phenomenon", color=COLOR_GIBBS, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(gibbs_text, "F4")
        
        self.play(

        )

class Section7Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Configuration
        TITLE = "Summary: Efficiency through Geometry"
        LINES = [
            "Pure series exploit the inherent symmetry of physical systems.",
            "Symmetry reduces our computational work by half.",
            "Elegant geometry makes complex math much more efficient."
        ]
        
        # Colors based on storyboard/lecture consistency
        COLOR_COMPLEX = WHITE
        COLOR_SIMPLE = WHITE
        COLOR_SAVING = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_STRING = "#ADD8E6"
        COLOR_FINAL = WHITE

        self.setup_layout(TITLE, LINES)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Complex formula vs Simple formula
        # Storyboard: "Left: Complex formula vs Right: Simple formula (#FFFFFF)."
        # Using symmetrical positioning (Belief B040) around midline x=3.0
        complex_tex = MathTex(
            r"f(x) = a_0 + \sum_{n=1}^\infty \left[ a_n \cos\left(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\right) + b_n \sin\left(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\right) \right]",
            color=COLOR_COMPLEX
        )
        simple_tex = MathTex(
            r"f(x) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty b_n \sin\left(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\right)",
            color=COLOR_SIMPLE
        )
        
        # Place symmetrically: Complex in B2-C3 (center x=2.0), Simple in B4-C5 (center x=4.0)
        # Avoid column 1 to respect B021
        self.place_in_area(complex_tex, "B2", "C3", scale_factor=0.35)
        self.place_in_area(simple_tex, "B4", "C5", scale_factor=0.45)
        
        vs_label = Text("vs", color=WHITE, font_size=20)
        # Place vs at the midline x=3.0 (between col 3 and 4)
        self.place_in_area(vs_label, "B3", "B4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_COMPLEX)
        self.play(
            Write(complex_tex), 
            Write(vs_label), 
            Write(simple_tex), 
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # '50% Less Math' label appears on the right
        # Storyboard: "'50% Less Math' label appears on the right (#00FF00)."
        less_math_label = Text("50% Less Math", color=COLOR_SAVING, font_size=24)
        # Positioned below the simple formula (col 4/5)
        self.place_at_grid(less_math_label, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        arrow = Arrow(
            start=simple_tex.get_bottom(),
            end=less_math_label.get_top(),
            color=COLOR_SAVING,
            buff=0.1
        )
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_SAVING)
        self.play(FadeIn(less_math_label), Create(arrow), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # A vibrating string animation shows physical symmetry
        # Storyboard: "A vibrating string animation shows physical symmetry (#ADD8E6)."
        # Symmetrical area E2 to F5 (x=1.5 to 4.5, center x=3.0)
        start_p = self.grid["E2"]
        end_p = self.grid["E5"]
        L_dist = end_p[0] - start_p[0]
        
        amp_tracker = ValueTracker(0.4)
        
        # Create a VMobject for the string and update points in place (efficient)
        string_mobj = VMobject(color=COLOR_STRING)
        def update_string(mob):
            amp = amp_tracker.get_value()
            points = [
                np.array([
                    start_p[0] + x * L_dist, 
                    start_p[1] + amp * np.sin(PI * x), 
                    0
                ])
                for x in np.linspace(0, 1, 40)
            ]
            mob.set_points_as_corners(points).make_smooth()

        update_string(string_mobj)
        string_mobj.add_updater(update_string)
        
        # Endpoints of the string (respect B001 - no overlap with formulas)
        dot_l = Dot(start_p, color=WHITE, radius=0.06)
        dot_r = Dot(end_p, color=WHITE, radius=0.06)
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_STRING)
        self.play(Create(dot_l), Create(dot_r), Create(string_mobj))
        
        # Vibration cycles using ValueTracker
        self.play(amp_tracker.animate.set_value(-0.4), run_time=0.8, rate_func=sine_merge)
        self.play(amp_tracker.animate.set_value(0.4), run_time=0.8, rate_func=sine_merge)
        
        # Closing text: 'Symmetry is efficiency' (#FFFFFF)
        closing_text = Text("Symmetry is efficiency", color=COLOR_FINAL, font_size=28)
        self.place_in_area(closing_text, "F2", "F5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(closing_text))
        
        # Final vibration and settle during conclusion
        self.play(amp_tracker.animate.set_value(-0.4), run_time=0.8, rate_func=sine_merge)
        self.play(amp_tracker.animate.set_value(0.4), run_time=0.8, rate_func=sine_merge)
        self.play(amp_tracker.animate.set_value(0), run_time=1.0, rate_func=smooth)
        
        self.wait(3)

section_1.title: The Hook: The Whistle-Bot's Pure Tones
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of complex periodic signals by using a 'Whistle-Bot' character. Explain that while most sounds are messy, the Whistle-Bot only understands pure, smooth oscillations (Sines and Cosines). The goal is to recreate a jagged 'Square Wave' jump using only these smooth movements.
section_1.example: Visualizing a Whistle-Bot moving up and down in a jerky square pattern, then overlaying smooth sine waves to show the approximation.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Full Fourier Recipe
section_2.content: Briefly review the Standard Fourier Series formula. Explain that any periodic function f(x) is a 'stew' of a constant (a0), Cosines (an), and Sines (bn). Emphasize the concept of 'Orthogonality'—that sines and cosines are like independent building blocks that don't mix.
section_2.example: An animation of a kitchen blender where 'Cosine Carrots' and 'Sine Spinneys' are tossed in to create a 'Function Soup'.

section_3.title: The Symmetry Filter: Even and Odd Functions
section_3.content: Introduce symmetry as a way to simplify the 'stew'. Define Even functions (f(x) = f(-x)) as mirror reflections across the Y-axis and Odd functions (f(x) = -f(-x)) as rotational symmetry. Explain that Cosine is the 'Even King' and Sine is the 'Odd Queen'.
section_3.example: A 'Symmetry Cat' sitting on the Y-axis. If the cat looks at a mirror and sees itself exactly, it's Even (Cosine-like). If it sees itself upside down on the other side, it's Odd (Sine-like).

section_4.title: Deriving the Pure Sine Series
section_4.content: Explain that if a function is Odd, all 'Even' components (Cosines) must have coefficients of zero (an = 0). This results in a 'Pure Sine Series'. Show the simplified integral formula for bn, noting that we only need to integrate over half the period (0 to L) and multiply by 2.
section_4.example: A visual 'mathematical sieve' where a jagged Odd Wave passes through, trapping all Cosine terms in the mesh and letting only Sine terms flow through to the final equation.

section_5.title: Deriving the Pure Cosine Series
section_5.content: Conversely, if the function is Even, all 'Odd' components (Sines) vanish (bn = 0). This creates a 'Pure Cosine Series'. Highlight that the constant term a0 (the average value) remains here because a constant is also an 'Even' function.
section_5.example: A graph of a 'Tent Map' function (Even). Watch the Sine waves try to fit but fail due to symmetry, leaving only the 'flat' a0 and the 'peaky' Cosines to reconstruct the shape.

section_6.title: Application: Building the Square Wave
section_6.content: Step-by-step calculation of a Pure Sine Series for a Square Wave (an Odd function). Show how adding the 1st, 3rd, and 5th harmonics gradually transforms a smooth wave into a sharp square corner.
section_6.example: An animation of the 'Square-Wave Robot' from Section 1. As we add more Sine terms (1/n terms), the robot's path becomes flatter on top and steeper at the edges, demonstrating the Gibbs Phenomenon at the corners.

section_7.title: Summary: Efficiency through Geometry
section_7.content: Wrap up by emphasizing that Pure Fourier Series aren't just 'shorter' math; they represent the inherent physical symmetry of a system (like a vibrating string fixed at both ends).
section_7.example: A split-screen view: One side shows a messy full equation, the other shows the elegant, 'Pure' version, highlighting the 50% reduction in computational effort.

section_1.title: The Hook: The Whistle-Bot's Pure Tones
lecture_lines: Meet Whistle-Bot, a master of pure periodic tones.
Most sounds are messy, but Whistle-Bot prefers smooth oscillations.
He moves in a jerky, jagged square wave pattern.
Can we recreate this jump using only smooth movements?
Let's explore the power of mathematical symmetry.
animations: Whistle-Bot moves in a jerky square pattern (#FFD700).
A single smooth Sine wave appears (#ADD8E6).
Whistle-Bot's path is overlaid with the Sine wave.
Second harmonic Sine wave joins the sum (#90EE90).
Resulting wave starts looking like the square path.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Full Fourier Recipe
lecture_lines: Every periodic function is a mathematical "stew" of waves.
The recipe includes constants, cosines, and sine components.
These building blocks are independent and do not mix.
animations: Full Fourier formula appears in the center (#FFFFFF).
Highlight a0 in yellow (#FFFF00).
Highlight Cosine terms in blue (#0000FF).
Highlight Sine terms in green (#00FF00).
Icons for Sine and Cosine remain separate (Orthogonality).

section_3.title: The Symmetry Filter: Even and Odd Functions
lecture_lines: Symmetry simplifies our mathematical "stew" significantly.
Even functions mirror perfectly across the vertical axis.
Odd functions exhibit rotational symmetry through the origin.
Cosines are the "Even Kings" of the wave world.
Sines serve as the "Odd Queens" in our series.
animations: Parabola y=x^2 mirrors across the Y-axis (#ADD8E6).
Cubic y=x^3 rotates 180 degrees through origin (#90EE90).
'Even King' Cosine graph flashes on the left (#ADD8E6).
'Odd Queen' Sine graph flashes on the right (#90EE90).

section_4.title: Deriving the Pure Sine Series
lecture_lines: For odd functions, all cosine terms vanish to zero.
We are left with a pure sine series representation.
Integration only requires half the period, then double it.
animations: Odd Square Wave enters a 'Cosine Filter' box (#FFFFFF).
Cosine terms (an) are ejected from the filter (#FF0000).
an = 0 text appears in bold (#FF0000).
Formula for bn fades in with 2/L highlighted (#FFFF00).

section_5.title: Deriving the Pure Cosine Series
lecture_lines: For even functions, all sine terms disappear completely.
This creates a pure cosine series for the function.
The constant average value, a0, remains an even component.
animations: Even Triangle Wave enters a 'Sine Filter' box (#FFFFFF).
Sine terms (bn) are ejected from the filter (#FF0000).
bn = 0 text appears in bold (#FF0000).
a0 (average value) stays with the Cosine terms (#FFFF00).

section_6.title: Application: Building the Square Wave
lecture_lines: Let's build a square wave using our sine series.
Adding the first harmonic creates a basic smooth curve.
Higher odd harmonics sharpen the corners of the wave.
With enough terms, a jagged square shape emerges.
Watch the "ears" appear at the edges—the Gibbs Phenomenon.
animations: Plot y = sin(x) (fundamental frequency) (#ADD8E6).
Add y = 1/3 sin(3x) to the graph (#90EE90).
Add y = 1/5 sin(5x) to the graph (#FFFF00).
Highlight the 'ripples' near the jump (Gibbs Phenomenon) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ears.svg].

section_7.title: Summary: Efficiency through Geometry
lecture_lines: Pure series exploit the inherent symmetry of physical systems.
Symmetry reduces our computational work by half.
Elegant geometry makes complex math much more efficient.
animations: Left: Complex formula vs Right: Simple formula (#FFFFFF).

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title_text = "The Hook: The Whistle-Bot's Pure Tones"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Meet Whistle-Bot, a master of pure periodic tones.",
            "- Most sounds are messy, but Whistle-Bot prefers smooth oscillations.",
            "- He moves in a jerky, jagged square wave pattern.",
            "- Can we recreate this jump using only smooth movements?",
            "- Let's explore the power of mathematical symmetry."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        BOT_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        SINE_COLOR = "#ADD8E6"
        HARMONIC_COLOR = "#90EE90"
        
        # Setup Axes in the grid area
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4 * PI, PI],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            tips=False,
            axis_config={"include_numbers": False, "color": GREY}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E6")
        
        # Whistle-Bot representation
        bot_body = Square(side_length=0.4, color=BOT_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.8)
        bot_head = Circle(radius=0.15, color=BOT_COLOR, fill_opacity=1).next_to(bot_body, UP, buff=0.05)
        bot_eye1 = Dot(radius=0.03, color=BLACK).move_to(bot_head.get_center() + 0.05 * LEFT + 0.02 * UP)
        bot_eye2 = Dot(radius=0.03, color=BLACK).move_to(bot_head.get_center() + 0.05 * RIGHT + 0.02 * UP)
        whistle_bot = VGroup(bot_body, bot_head, bot_eye1, bot_eye2).scale(0.6)
        
        # ValueTracker for movement
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BOT_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(whistle_bot, "C4")
        self.play(FadeIn(whistle_bot))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(SINE_COLOR)
        self.play(Create(axes))
        
        sine_func = lambda x: np.sin(x)
        sine_wave = axes.plot(sine_func, color=SINE_COLOR)
        self.play(Create(sine_wave))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(sine_wave))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BOT_COLOR)
        
        square_wave_func = lambda x: 1.0 if np.sin(x) >= 0 else -1.0
        square_wave = axes.plot(
            square_wave_func, 
            color=BOT_COLOR, 
            use_smoothing=False, 
            discontinuities=[PI, 2*PI, 3*PI]
        )
        
        # Attach bot to the square wave path
        whistle_bot.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(axes.c2p(time_tracker.get_value(), square_wave_func(time_tracker.get_value()))))
        
        self.play(Create(square_wave))
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(4 * PI), run_time=5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(SINE_COLOR)
        
        # Fundamental component of Fourier series for square wave: (4/pi) * sin(x)
        fundamental_func = lambda x: (4/PI) * np.sin(x)
        fundamental_wave = axes.plot(fundamental_func, color=SINE_COLOR)
        
        # Overlaying the first smooth movement
        self.play(Create(fundamental_wave))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(HARMONIC_COLOR)
        
        # Second harmonic (third term in series): (4/(3*pi)) * sin(3x)
        third_harmonic_func = lambda x: (4/(3*PI)) * np.sin(3*x)
        third_harmonic_wave = axes.plot(third_harmonic_func, color=HARMONIC_COLOR)
        
        # The sum of the two
        sum_func = lambda x: fundamental_func(x) + third_harmonic_func(x)
        sum_wave = axes.plot(sum_func, color=WHITE)
        
        self.play(Create(third_harmonic_wave))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Show the result of summing them
        self.play(
            FadeOut(fundamental_wave),
            FadeOut(third_harmonic_wave),
            Create(sum_wave)
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final cleanup: Remove updater to prevent errors at the end of the scene
        whistle_bot.clear_updaters()

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Prerequisite: The Full Fourier Recipe"
        lines = [
            "Every periodic function is a mathematical \"stew\" of waves.",
            "The recipe includes constants, cosines, and sine components.",
            "These building blocks are independent and do not mix."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        YELLOW_A = "#FFFF00"
        BLUE_B = "#0000FF"
        GREEN_C = "#00FF00"
        WHITE_CLR = "#FFFFFF"
        GRAY_CLR = "#888888"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Every periodic function is a mathematical "stew" of waves.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE_CLR)
        
        # Full Fourier formula
        # Split into parts for specific highlighting
        # f(x) = a0 + sum ( an cos(nx) + bn sin(nx) )
        formula = MathTex(
            "f(x)", "=", "a_0", "+", "\\sum_{n=1}^{\\infty}", 
            "(", "a_n \\cos(nx)", "+", "b_n \\sin(nx)", ")"
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The recipe includes constants, cosines, and sine components.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY_CLR),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE_CLR)
        )
        
        # Highlight a0 in yellow, Cosine terms in blue, Sine terms in green
        self.play(
            formula[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW_A),
            formula[6].animate.set_color(BLUE_B),
            formula[8].animate.set_color(GREEN_C),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # These building blocks are independent and do not mix.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY_CLR),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE_CLR)
        )
        
        # Show orthogonality by separating Sine and Cosine icons
        # Creating simple blocks to represent them
        cos_block = VGroup(
            RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.8, width=1.5, color=BLUE_B),
            MathTex("\\cos(nx)", color=BLUE_B).scale(0.7)
        )
        sin_block = VGroup(
            RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.8, width=1.5, color=GREEN_C),
            MathTex("\\sin(nx)", color=GREEN_C).scale(0.7)
        )
        
        self.place_at_grid(cos_block, 'E2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(sin_block, 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Add labels for independence
        indep_label = Text("Independent", font_size=18, color=WHITE_CLR)
        self.place_at_grid(indep_label, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)

        # Transition from formula to blocks
        self.play(
            formula.animate.scale(0.6).move_to(self.grid['B3']),
            FadeIn(cos_block),
            FadeIn(sin_block),
            Write(indep_label)
        )
        
        # Show they don't mix by pulsing them separately
        self.play(cos_block.animate.scale(1.1), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(cos_block.animate.scale(1/1.1), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(sin_block.animate.scale(1.1), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(sin_block.animate.scale(1/1.1), run_time=0.5)
        
        self.wait(3)

        # Colors
        COLOR_EVEN = "#ADD8E6"
        COLOR_ODD = "#90EE90"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Symmetry simplifies our mathematical "stew" significantly.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Even functions mirror perfectly across the vertical axis.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_EVEN))
        
        axes_even = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            x_length=2.0,
            y_length=1.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": GREY, "stroke_width": 2}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes_even, "B1", "C3")
        
        label_even = Text("Even (y=x²)", color=COLOR_EVEN, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label_even, "A2")
        
        parabola_right = axes_even.plot(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[0, 2], color=COLOR_EVEN)
        parabola_left = axes_even.plot(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[-2, 0], color=COLOR_EVEN)
        
        self.play(Create(axes_even), Write(label_even))
        self.play(Create(parabola_right))
        
        # Mirroring animation: transform a copy across the y-axis
        parabola_mirror = parabola_right.copy()
        # Scale by -1 on x-axis relative to axis center
        mirror_matrix = [[-1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0, 0, 1]]
        self.play(
            parabola_mirror.animate.apply_matrix(mirror_matrix, about_point=axes_even.c2p(0, 0, 0)),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.add(parabola_left)
        self.remove(parabola_mirror)

        cubic_right = axes_odd.plot(lambda x: x**3, x_range=[0, 1.5], color=COLOR_ODD)
        cubic_left = axes_odd.plot(lambda x: x**3, x_range=[-1.5, 0], color=COLOR_ODD)
        
        self.play(Create(axes_odd), Write(label_odd))
        self.play(Create(cubic_right))
        
        # Rotational symmetry animation: rotate 180 degrees through origin
        cubic_rotation = cubic_right.copy()
        self.play(
            Rotate(cubic_rotation, angle=PI, about_point=axes_odd.c2p(0, 0, 0)),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.add(cubic_left)
        self.remove(cubic_rotation)
        self.wait(1)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup data
        title = "Application: Building the Square Wave"
        lines = [
            "Let's build a square wave using our sine series.",
            "Adding the first harmonic creates a basic smooth curve.",
            "Higher odd harmonics sharpen the corners of the wave.",
            "With enough terms, a jagged square shape emerges.",
            "Watch the \"ears\" appear at the edges—the Gibbs Phenomenon."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_H1 = "#ADD8E6"  # Light Blue
        COLOR_H3 = "#90EE90"  # Light Green
        COLOR_H5 = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        COLOR_SUM = WHITE
        COLOR_GIBBS = RED

        # Axes setup
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-1.1 * PI, 1.1 * PI, PI / 2],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=4.0,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GRAY},
            tips=False
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "F6")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Let's build a square wave using our sine series."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(Create(axes), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Adding the first harmonic creates a basic smooth curve."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_H1)
        
        func_h1 = lambda x: np.sin(x)
        graph_current = axes.plot(func_h1, color=COLOR_H1)
        label_current = MathTex("S_1(x) = \\sin(x)", color=COLOR_H1, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(label_current, "A4")
        
        self.play(Create(graph_current), Write(label_current))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Higher odd harmonics sharpen the corners of the wave."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_H3)
        
        # Step 1: n=3
        func_h3 = lambda x: np.sin(x) + (1/3) * np.sin(3*x)
        graph_h3 = axes.plot(func_h3, color=COLOR_H3)
        label_h3 = MathTex("S_3(x) = \\sin(x) + \\frac{1}{3}\\sin(3x)", color=COLOR_H3, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(label_h3, "A4")
        
        self.play(
            Transform(graph_current, graph_h3),
            Transform(label_current, label_h3),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Step 2: n=5
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_H5)
        func_h5 = lambda x: np.sin(x) + (1/3) * np.sin(3*x) + (1/5) * np.sin(5*x)
        graph_h5 = axes.plot(func_h5, color=COLOR_H5)
        label_h5 = MathTex("S_5(x) = \\sum_{n=1,3,5} \\frac{1}{n}\\sin(nx)", color=COLOR_H5, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(label_h5, "A4")
        
        self.play(
            Transform(graph_current, graph_h5),
            Transform(label_current, label_h5),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "With enough terms, a jagged square shape emerges."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        
        def fourier_sum_n(x, n_max):
            return sum([(1/k) * np.sin(k*x) for k in range(1, n_max + 1, 2)])

        func_h19 = lambda x: fourier_sum_n(x, 19)
        graph_h19 = axes.plot(func_h19, color=COLOR_SUM)
        label_h19 = MathTex("S_{19}(x) = \\sum_{n=1,3,\\dots,19} \\frac{1}{n}\\sin(nx)", color=COLOR_SUM, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(label_h19, "A4")
        
        self.play(
            Transform(graph_current, graph_h19),
            Transform(label_current, label_h19),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "Watch the \"ears\" appear at the edges—the Gibbs Phenomenon."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_GIBBS)
        
        # Highlighting the overshoot "ears"
        ripples = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.15, color=COLOR_GIBBS).move_to(axes.c2p(0.1, 1.2)),
            Circle(radius=0.15, color=COLOR_GIBBS).move_to(axes.c2p(-0.1, -1.2)),
            Circle(radius=0.15, color=COLOR_GIBBS).move_to(axes.c2p(PI-0.1, 1.2)),
            Circle(radius=0.15, color=COLOR_GIBBS).move_to(axes.c2p(-PI+0.1, -1.2))
        )
        
        gibbs_text = Text("Gibbs Phenomenon", color=COLOR_GIBBS, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(gibbs_text, "F4")
        
        self.play(
            Create(ripples),
            Write(gibbs_text)
        )
        self.wait(4)

class Section7Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Configuration
        TITLE = "Summary: Efficiency through Geometry"
        LINES = [
            "Pure series exploit the inherent symmetry of physical systems.",
            "Symmetry reduces our computational work by half.",
            "Elegant geometry makes complex math much more efficient."
        ]
        
        # Colors based on storyboard/lecture consistency
        COLOR_COMPLEX = WHITE
        COLOR_SIMPLE = WHITE
        COLOR_SAVING = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_STRING = "#ADD8E6"
        COLOR_FINAL = WHITE

        self.setup_layout(TITLE, LINES)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        complex_tex = MathTex(
            r"f(x) = a_0 + \sum_{n=1}^\infty \left[ a_n \cos\left(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\right) + b_n \sin\left(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\right) \right]",
            color=COLOR_COMPLEX
        )
        simple_tex = MathTex(
            r"f(x) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty b_n \sin\left(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\right)",
            color=COLOR_SIMPLE
        )
        
        self.place_in_area(complex_tex, "B2", "C3", scale_factor=0.35)
        self.place_in_area(simple_tex, "B4", "C5", scale_factor=0.45)
        
        vs_label = Text("vs", color=WHITE, font_size=20)
        self.place_in_area(vs_label, "B3", "B4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_COMPLEX)
        self.play(
            Write(complex_tex), 
            Write(vs_label), 
            Write(simple_tex), 
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        less_math_label = Text("50% Less Math", color=COLOR_SAVING, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(less_math_label, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        arrow = Arrow(
            start=simple_tex.get_bottom(),
            end=less_math_label.get_top(),
            color=COLOR_SAVING,
            buff=0.1
        )
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_SAVING)
        self.play(FadeIn(less_math_label), Create(arrow), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        start_p = self.grid["E2"]
        end_p = self.grid["E5"]
        L_dist = end_p[0] - start_p[0]
        
        amp_tracker = ValueTracker(0.4)
        
        string_mobj = VMobject(color=COLOR_STRING)
        def update_string(mob):
            amp = amp_tracker.get_value()
            points = [
                np.array([
                    start_p[0] + x * L_dist, 
                    start_p[1] + amp * np.sin(PI * x), 
                    0
                ])
                for x in np.linspace(0, 1, 40)
            ]
            mob.set_points_as_corners(points).make_smooth()

        update_string(string_mobj)
        string_mobj.add_updater(update_string)
        
        dot_l = Dot(start_p, color=WHITE, radius=0.06)
        dot_r = Dot(end_p, color=WHITE, radius=0.06)
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_STRING)
        self.play(Create(dot_l), Create(dot_r), Create(string_mobj))
        
        # Vibration cycles using ValueTracker - replaced sine_merge with smooth
        self.play(amp_tracker.animate.set_value(-0.4), run_time=0.8, rate_func=smooth)
        self.play(amp_tracker.animate.set_value(0.4), run_time=0.8, rate_func=smooth)
        
        # Closing text: 'Symmetry is efficiency' (#FFFFFF)
        closing_text = Text("Symmetry is efficiency", color=COLOR_FINAL, font_size=28)

outline.title: The Symmetry Filter: Even and Odd Functions
outline.content: Introduce symmetry as a way to simplify the 'stew'. Define Even functions (f(x) = f(-x)) as mirror reflections across the Y-axis and Odd functions (f(x) = -f(-x)) as rotational symmetry. Explain that Cosine is the 'Even King' and Sine is the 'Odd Queen'.
outline.example: A 'Symmetry Cat' sitting on the Y-axis. If the cat looks at a mirror and sees itself exactly, it's Even (Cosine-like). If it sees itself upside down on the other side, it's Odd (Sine-like).

storyboard.title: The Symmetry Filter: Even and Odd Functions
lecture_lines: Symmetry simplifies our mathematical "stew" significantly.
Even functions mirror perfectly across the vertical axis.
Odd functions exhibit rotational symmetry through the origin.
Cosines are the "Even Kings" of the wave world.
Sines serve as the "Odd Queens" in our series.
animations: Parabola y=x^2 mirrors across the Y-axis (#ADD8E6).
Cubic y=x^3 rotates 180 degrees through origin (#90EE90).
'Even King' Cosine graph flashes on the left (#ADD8E6).
'Odd Queen' Sine graph flashes on the right (#90EE90).

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Symmetry simplifies our mathematical \"stew\" significantly.",
            "Even functions mirror perfectly across the vertical axis.",
            "Odd functions exhibit rotational symmetry through the origin.",
            "Cosines are the \"Even Kings\" of the wave world.",
            "Sines serve as the \"Odd Queens\" in our series."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Symmetry Filter: Even and Odd Functions", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_EVEN = "#ADD8E6"
        COLOR_ODD = "#90EE90"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Symmetry simplifies our mathematical "stew" significantly.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Even functions mirror perfectly across the vertical axis.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_EVEN))
        
        axes_even = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            x_length=2.0,
            y_length=1.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": GREY, "stroke_width": 2}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes_even, "B1", "C3")
        
        label_even = Text("Even (y=x²)", color=COLOR_EVEN, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label_even, "A2")
        
        parabola_right = axes_even.plot(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[0, 2], color=COLOR_EVEN)
        parabola_left = axes_even.plot(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[-2, 0], color=COLOR_EVEN)
        
        self.play(Create(axes_even), Write(label_even))
        self.play(Create(parabola_right))
        
        # Mirroring animation: transform a copy across the y-axis
        parabola_mirror = parabola_right.copy()
        # Scale by -1 on x-axis relative to axis center
        mirror_matrix = [[-1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0, 0, 1]]
        self.play(
            parabola_mirror.animate.apply_matrix(mirror_matrix, about_point=axes_even.c2p(0, 0, 0)),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.add(parabola_left)
        self.remove(parabola_mirror)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Odd functions exhibit rotational symmetry through the origin.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_ODD))
        
        axes_odd = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-4, 4, 2],
            x_length=2.0,
            y_length=1.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": GREY, "stroke_width": 2}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes_odd, "B4", "C6")
        
        label_odd = Text("Odd (y=x³)", color=COLOR_ODD, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label_odd, "A5")
        
        cubic_right = axes_odd.plot(lambda x: x**3, x_range=[0, 1.5], color=COLOR_ODD)
        cubic_left = axes_odd.plot(lambda x: x**3, x_range=[-1.5, 0], color=COLOR_ODD)
        
        self.play(Create(axes_odd), Write(label_odd))
        self.play(Create(cubic_right))
        
        # Rotational symmetry animation: rotate 180 degrees through origin
        cubic_rotation = cubic_right.copy()
        self.play(
            Rotate(cubic_rotation, angle=PI, about_point=axes_odd.c2p(0, 0, 0)),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.add(cubic_left)
        self.remove(cubic_rotation)

lecture_lines: For even functions, all sine terms disappear completely.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Deriving the Pure Cosine Series"
        lines = [
            "For even functions, all sine terms disappear completely.",
            "This creates a pure cosine series for the function.",
            "The constant average value, a0, remains an even component."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        filter_color = "#FFFFFF"
        bn_color = "#FF0000"
        a0_color = "#FFFF00"
        cosine_color = "#00FFFF" # Light cyan for cosines

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(filter_color))

        # Create Sine Filter Box
        filter_box = Rectangle(width=2, height=1.5, color=filter_color)
        filter_text = Text("Sine Filter", font_size=18, color=filter_color)
        sine_filter = VGroup(filter_box, filter_text)
        self.place_in_area(sine_filter, "B3", "D4")
        
        # Create Even Triangle Wave
        triangle_wave = VMobject(color=WHITE)
        triangle_wave.set_points_as_corners([
            [-0.5, -0.5, 0], [0, 0.5, 0], [0.5, -0.5, 0]
        ])
        self.place_at_grid(triangle_wave, "C2")

        self.play(FadeIn(sine_filter))
        self.play(FadeIn(triangle_wave))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Move triangle wave into filter
        self.play(
            triangle_wave.animate.move_to(sine_filter.get_center()).scale(0.5).set_alpha(0),
            run_time=1.5
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(bn_color))

        # Sine terms (bn) ejected from the filter
        sine_icon = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.3 * np.sin(2 * PI * x), x_range=[-0.5, 0.5], color=bn_color)
        bn_label = MathTex("b_n = 0", color=bn_color).scale(0.8)
        
        self.place_at_grid(sine_icon, "C4")
        self.place_at_grid(bn_label, "E4")

        # Animate ejection
        self.play(
            sine_icon.animate.move_to(self.grid["E4"]),
            FadeIn(bn_label, target_position=self.grid["E4"]),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(FadeOut(sine_icon))

        # Cosine terms emerge from the right
        cosine_icon = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.3 * np.cos(2 * PI * x), x_range=[-0.5, 0.5], color=cosine_color)
        self.place_at_grid(cosine_icon, "C5")
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(cosine_icon, shift=RIGHT),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(a0_color))

        # a0 remains with the cosine terms
        a0_label = MathTex("a_0", color=a0_color).scale(0.8)
        a0_line = Line(start=[-0.4, 0, 0], end=[0.4, 0, 0], color=a0_color)
        a0_group = VGroup(a0_line, a0_label).arrange(UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(a0_group, "D5")

        self.play(
            FadeIn(a0_group, shift=UP),
            cosine_icon.animate.shift(UP * 0.2), # Small adjustment to group them
            run_time=1
        )
        
        # Group result
        result_group = VGroup(cosine_icon, a0_group)
        rect_highlight = SurroundingRectangle(result_group, color=WHITE, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(rect_highlight))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Hook: The Whistle-Bot's Pure Tones
outline.content: Introduce the concept of complex periodic signals by using a 'Whistle-Bot' character. Explain that while most sounds are messy, the Whistle-Bot only understands pure, smooth oscillations (Sines and Cosines). The goal is to recreate a jagged 'Square Wave' jump using only these smooth movements.
outline.example: Visualizing a Whistle-Bot moving up and down in a jerky square pattern, then overlaying smooth sine waves to show the approximation.

storyboard.title: The Hook: The Whistle-Bot's Pure Tones
lecture_lines: Meet Whistle-Bot, a master of pure periodic tones.
Most sounds are messy, but Whistle-Bot prefers smooth oscillations.
He moves in a jerky, jagged square wave pattern.
Can we recreate this jump using only smooth movements?
Let's explore the power of mathematical symmetry.
animations: Whistle-Bot moves in a jerky square pattern (#FFD700).
A single smooth Sine wave appears (#ADD8E6).
Whistle-Bot's path is overlaid with the Sine wave.
Second harmonic Sine wave joins the sum (#90EE90).
Resulting wave starts looking like the square path.

            "- Let's explore the power of mathematical symmetry."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        BOT_COLOR = "#FFD700"
        SINE_COLOR = "#ADD8E6"
        HARMONIC_COLOR = "#90EE90"
        
        # Setup Axes in the grid area
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4 * PI, PI],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            tips=False,
            axis_config={"include_numbers": False, "color": GREY}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E6")
        
        # Whistle-Bot representation
        bot_body = Square(side_length=0.4, color=BOT_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.8)
        bot_head = Circle(radius=0.15, color=BOT_COLOR, fill_opacity=1).next_to(bot_body, UP, buff=0.05)
        bot_eye1 = Dot(radius=0.03, color=BLACK).move_to(bot_head.get_center() + 0.05 * LEFT + 0.02 * UP)
        bot_eye2 = Dot(radius=0.03, color=BLACK).move_to(bot_head.get_center() + 0.05 * RIGHT + 0.02 * UP)
        whistle_bot = VGroup(bot_body, bot_head, bot_eye1, bot_eye2).scale(0.6)
        
        # ValueTracker for movement
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BOT_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(whistle_bot, "C4")
        self.play(FadeIn(whistle_bot))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(SINE_COLOR)
        self.play(Create(axes))
        
        sine_func = lambda x: np.sin(x)
        sine_wave = axes.plot(sine_func, color=SINE_COLOR)
        self.play(Create(sine_wave))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(sine_wave))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BOT_COLOR)
        
        square_wave_func = lambda x: 1.0 if np.sin(x) >= 0 else -1.0
        square_wave = axes.plot(
            square_wave_func, 
            color=BOT_COLOR, 
            use_smoothing=False, 
            discontinuities=[PI, 2*PI, 3*PI]
        )
        
        # Attach bot to the square wave path
        whistle_bot.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(axes.c2p(time_tracker.get_value(), square_wave_func(time_tracker.get_value()))))
        
        self.play(Create(square_wave))
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(4 * PI), run_time=5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(SINE_COLOR)
        
        # Fundamental component of Fourier series for square wave: (4/pi) * sin(x)
        fundamental_func = lambda x: (4/PI) * np.sin(x)
        fundamental_wave = axes.plot(fundamental_func, color=SINE_COLOR)
        
        # Overlaying the first smooth movement
        self.play(Create(fundamental_wave))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(HARMONIC_COLOR)
        
        # Second harmonic (third term in series): (4/(3*pi)) * sin(3x)
        third_harmonic_func = lambda x: (4/(3*PI)) * np.sin(3*x)
        third_harmonic_wave = axes.plot(third_harmonic_func, color=HARMONIC_COLOR)
        
        # The sum of the two
        sum_func = lambda x: fundamental_func(x) + third_harmonic_func(x)
        sum_wave = axes.plot(sum_func, color=WHITE)
        
        self.play(Create(third_harmonic_wave))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Show the result of summing them
        self.play(
            FadeOut(fundamental_wave),
            FadeOut(third_harmonic_wave),
            Create(sum_wave)
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final cleanup: Remove updater to prevent errors at the end of the scene
        whistle_bot.clear_updaters()

outline.title: Deriving the Pure Sine Series
outline.content: Explain that if a function is Odd, all 'Even' components (Cosines) must have coefficients of zero (an = 0). This results in a 'Pure Sine Series'. Show the simplified integral formula for bn, noting that we only need to integrate over half the period (0 to L) and multiply by 2.
outline.example: A visual 'mathematical sieve' where a jagged Odd Wave passes through, trapping all Cosine terms in the mesh and letting only Sine terms flow through to the final equation.

storyboard.title: Deriving the Pure Sine Series
lecture_lines: For odd functions, all cosine terms vanish to zero.
We are left with a pure sine series representation.
Integration only requires half the period, then double it.
animations: Odd Square Wave enters a 'Cosine Filter' box (#FFFFFF).
Cosine terms (an) are ejected from the filter (#FF0000).
an = 0 text appears in bold (#FF0000).
Formula for bn fades in with 2/L highlighted (#FFFF00).

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup layout with script content
        lecture_lines = [
            "For odd functions, all cosine terms vanish to zero.",
            "We are left with a pure sine series representation.",
            "Integration only requires half the period, then double it."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Deriving the Pure Sine Series", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight lecture line 1 in Red to match vanishing terms
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))

        # Odd Square Wave (Visual representative of an odd function)
        wave = VMobject(color=BLUE)
        wave_points = [
            [-1.5, 0.5, 0], [-1, 0.5, 0], [-1, -0.5, 0], [-0.5, -0.5, 0], 
            [-0.5, 0.5, 0], [0, 0.5, 0], [0, -0.5, 0], [0.5, -0.5, 0],
            [0.5, 0.5, 0], [1, 0.5, 0], [1, -0.5, 0], [1.5, -0.5, 0]
        ]
        wave.set_points_as_corners(wave_points)
        self.place_at_grid(wave, "C1", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Cosine Filter Box (#FFFFFF)
        filter_box = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=1.8, color=WHITE)
        filter_label = Text("Cosine Filter", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        filter_group = VGroup(filter_box, filter_label)
        self.place_in_area(filter_group, "B2", "D4")

        self.play(Create(filter_group), Create(wave))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Wave enters the box to be filtered
        self.play(wave.animate.move_to(self.grid["C3"]))

        # Cosine terms (an) ejected from the filter (#FF0000)
        an_symbols = VGroup(*[MathTex("a_n", color="#FF0000") for _ in range(3)])
        for sym in an_symbols:
            sym.move_to(self.grid["C3"])
        
        ejection_targets = ["B5", "C5", "D5"]
        ejection_anims = []
        for i in range(3):
            ejection_anims.append(
                Succession(
                    FadeIn(an_symbols[i]),
                    an_symbols[i].animate.move_to(self.grid[ejection_targets[i]]).set_opacity(0),
                    run_time=0.8
                )
            )
        
        self.play(AnimationGroup(*ejection_anims, lag_ratio=0.4))

        # an = 0 text appears in bold (#FF0000)
        an_zero = MathTex(r"a_n = 0", color="#FF0000", font_size=44)
        self.place_at_grid(an_zero, "D5")
        self.play(Write(an_zero))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Revert Line 1 color and maintain Line 2 white
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )

        # Pure sine series representation
        sine_series = MathTex(
            r"f(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} b_n \sin\left(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\right)",
            color=WHITE, font_size=36
        )
        # Position at the top of the animation area
        self.place_in_area(sine_series, "A1", "A6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(sine_series))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight lecture line 3 in Yellow to match bn highlight
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00")
        )

        # Formula for bn with 2/L and limits highlighted (#FFFF00)
        bn_parts = [
            r"b_n = ", r"\frac{2}{L}", r" \int", r"_{0}", r"^{L}", r" f(x) \sin\left(\frac{n\pi x}{L}\right) dx"
        ]
        bn_formula = MathTex(*bn_parts, color=WHITE, font_size=36)
        # Indices: 1 is 2/L, 3 is 0, 4 is L
        bn_formula[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        bn_formula[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        bn_formula[4].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Position at the bottom of the animation area
        self.place_in_area(bn_formula, "F1", "F6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(bn_formula))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: Application: Building the Square Wave
outline.content: Step-by-step calculation of a Pure Sine Series for a Square Wave (an Odd function). Show how adding the 1st, 3rd, and 5th harmonics gradually transforms a smooth wave into a sharp square corner.
outline.example: An animation of the 'Square-Wave Robot' from Section 1. As we add more Sine terms (1/n terms), the robot's path becomes flatter on top and steeper at the edges, demonstrating the Gibbs Phenomenon at the corners.

storyboard.title: Application: Building the Square Wave
lecture_lines: Let's build a square wave using our sine series.
Adding the first harmonic creates a basic smooth curve.
Higher odd harmonics sharpen the corners of the wave.
With enough terms, a jagged square shape emerges.
Watch the "ears" appear at the edges—the Gibbs Phenomenon.
animations: Plot y = sin(x) (fundamental frequency) (#ADD8E6).
Add y = 1/3 sin(3x) to the graph (#90EE90).
Add y = 1/5 sin(5x) to the graph (#FFFF00).
Highlight the 'ripples' near the jump (Gibbs Phenomenon) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ears.svg].
